items.title: AMD MI355X reaches up to 2x B200 performance per dollar on Kimi K3 agentic inference after kernel tuning
items.summary: SemiAnalysis reports AMD's software team got up to twice the tokens per dollar of a B200 server on Kimi K3 agentic serving, from tuned AITER kernels and MonoKernel decode in vLLM. The 2,304 GB of HBM per MI355X server keeps the model in one box, so decode avoids the cross-server network a B200 deployment needs.

doubt.pushback: Repliers note the result is one model hand-tuned by AMD, quoted as 'up to' (2.45x only at the fast end of the curve, about 1.7x at 20 tok/s per user), and ask for a GB200 NVL72 comparison where the whole model also fits in one domain.

reception.summary: Most replies credit software and the larger per-server HBM rather than the chip; a few read the chart (about 13% cheaper per chip-hour, so most of the gain is tokens per chip) and question whether the gap survives other models, longer contexts or NVL72.

items.title: Local-model agent benchmark by VRAM tier: a 12 GB card clears 27 of 30 Hermes Agent tasks, 32 GB clears all 30
items.summary: A 30-task offline agent suite in Hermes Agent (multi-file renames, merge conflicts, git bisect, fixing bugs behind a 40-test suite) picks the best quantized model for each GPU memory size at 64K context. Spark-X2.6-4B gets 25/30 on 8 GB, Ornith 1.5 9B 27/30 on 12 GB, and Qwen3.8-27B reaches 29/30 at Q4_K_M and 30/30 at Q6_K, with tool-call counts and wall times reported.

items.title: CMU paper: pretraining, midtraining, SFT and RL run as one likelihood-based 'unified training' algorithm
items.summary: The paper treats suitable RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated targets, so RL rollouts and static data share one loss and one trainer and staged training becomes a special case. In small experiments (124M from scratch, 0.76B on math RL) unified runs beat staged training on unseen larger puzzles and on retaining coding skill after math training; the authors found no single best data mix.

items.title: Browser Use ships Ultrafast, a low-latency web agent preset, to all US cloud plans
items.summary: Browser Use Cloud now offers an 'ultrafast' model preset without a waitlist; the team's real-time demo shows simple tasks finishing in under 3 seconds, a 14.4 s median and about $0.13 for 25 tasks. Speed and cost figures are the vendor's own, from the demo set.

doubt.pushback: Latency and cost numbers come only from the vendor's own 25-task demo video.

items.title: Mixdog: open-source coding agent matches Codex CLI on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with 63% fewer tokens
items.summary: Mixdog is an Apache-2.0 desktop coding agent where a lead model plans and cheaper models handle search, edits and review. Its authors report 86.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 over 445 trials with 157M tokens against Codex CLI's 86.1% with 421M tokens on the same model.

doubt.pushback: Self-reported benchmark from a no-reach post; not independently reproduced.

items.title: Galvanize 3: open-weight 140M multilingual prompt-injection classifier that runs on CPU
items.summary: zn released the weights of the classifier behind its API under Apache 2.0: about 140M parameters, multilingual and CPU-friendly, so agent builders can screen inputs for prompt injection locally. The team reports 89.6% of attacks caught at 0.6% false positives on its own 3,309-example test set.

doubt.pushback: Detection numbers are on the vendor's own test set.
